moved.sentence: Chunk documents before embedding; chunk size and overlap directly determine retrieval quality.

judged.note: Kept verbatim at SHOULD, including the reason that chunk size and overlap directly determine retrieval quality.

moved.sentence: There is no universal best size — start with a moderate window with small overlap and tune against a retrieval eval set.

judged.note: Kept verbatim at SHOULD: no universal best size, start with a moderate window and small overlap, tune against a retrieval eval set.

moved.sentence: Prefer chunking on semantic/structural boundaries (headings, paragraphs, code blocks) over fixed character counts where the source structure allows it.

judged.note: Kept verbatim at SHOULD, with the structural-boundary examples and the 'where the source structure allows it' condition.

moved.sentence: Treat that migration as a reversible, scale-triggered decision, not a default.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD, with 'that migration' made explicit as the migration to a dedicated vector database: reversible, scale-triggered, not a default.

moved.sentence: Use an **HNSW** index as the default.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: HNSW is the default vector index.

moved.sentence: It gives a better speed/recall tradeoff than IVFFlat and needs no training step; the cost is slower build time and higher memory. (Source: pgvector README, 2026.)

judged.note: Kept: rationale under should-default-to-hnsw carries the speed/recall tradeoff over IVFFlat, no training step and the build-time/memory cost; references cites the pgvector README (2026) as its source.

moved.sentence: Raise `ef_search` to trade latency for recall.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: raise `ef_search` to trade latency for recall; the default values it refers to stay in indexing.

moved.sentence: Verify current defaults against the pinned pgvector version before relying on them.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD: verify the current defaults against the pinned pgvector version before relying on them; the HNSW defaults it refers to stay in indexing.

moved.sentence: Pick the distance operator that matches how the embedding model was trained — cosine (`<=>`) for most normalized text embeddings, inner product (`<#>`) or L2 (`<->`) when the model specifies it.

judged.note: Kept verbatim at SHOULD with all three operators and when each applies.

moved.sentence: **MUST** be consistent between indexing and querying.

judged.note: Kept at MUST, with the subject (the distance operator) made explicit: consistent between indexing and querying.

moved.sentence: Store filterable attributes (tenant, source, document type, timestamp, access scope) as ordinary columns alongside the vector, and filter on them in the same query.

judged.note: Kept verbatim at SHOULD with the full list of filterable attributes and the same-query filter.
Kept at SHOULD and expanded to name the four steps (dense, lexical, fusion, optional rerank), which stay listed in prefer-hybrid-retrieval-over-pure-ann; the pure-ANN reason is kept in rationale.

moved.sentence: The dense-vs-lexical balance is workload-dependent and contested — treat fusion weights and whether to rerank as things to measure on your own eval set, not as fixed constants.

judged.note: Kept verbatim at SHOULD: the dense-vs-lexical balance is workload-dependent and contested, fusion weights and reranking are measured on your own eval set, not fixed constants.
